tagline: Two tries at the Main Street Across America, meeting at Valparaiso.
intro: The Lincoln Highway, the first named automobile road across the country, was the idea of Carl G. Fisher of Indianapolis, and it was dedicated on October 31, 1913. In Indiana it ran two ways. The original road came in from Ohio through Fort Wayne and swung north through Churubusco, Ligonier, Goshen, Elkhart, South Bend and La Porte. The later, more direct line went by Columbia City, Warsaw and Plymouth. The two meet at Valparaiso and go on together to the Illinois line at Dyer.
In 1913 many cars had neither a speedometer nor an odometer, so control stations along the way helped travelers keep count of the miles. Plenty of towns renamed their main street Lincolnway.

moments.title: Churubusco
moments.text: Named for a Mexican battlefield because no other Indiana town was likely to have it, the town drew crowds in 1949 to a farm lake after a giant snapping turtle nobody ever caught.

moments.title: Goshen
moments.text: Yankee settlers who counted themselves a chosen people laid out the town in 1831 and named it for the Land of Goshen.

moments.title: Valparaiso
moments.text: The two routes come together in a county seat that started as Portersville and was renamed in 1837 for the Chilean port where the county's namesake, David Porter, fought a battle.
